result: Actual pixels support a two-yod divine-name abbreviation at Hebrew Psalm 77:8 (POB 77:7), locally different from the MT Adonai spelling and from an alef/dalet abbreviation at Hebrew 77:3. This is not four preserved consonants יהוה and does not establish the exemplar's spelling or historical priority. Retain current POB/base provisionally; no application.

record.consultation: Complete institutional TEI read; manifest and both image canvases inspected. TEI body contains page-break pointers, no diplomatic transcription.
record.catalogue_genre: Shorthand Hebrew Bible, serugin focused on initial syllables; usually at least two letters per word

record.language: Hebrew with Tiberian vocalisation and cantillation
record.published_claim: Catalogue identifies an abbreviated Tetragrammaton at Psalm 77:8 where MT has אדני.

target.line_count_basis: Visible main text rows counted from top, including heading rows but excluding small quire numeral; line locator is this report's, not an edition line number.
target.anchor: Divine sign between abbreviated יזנ and ול; preceding row has Psalm 77:7 context; ensuing text enters 77:9.

observations.basis: Source-native regional pixels, context-informed single agent
observations.qualification: Two yod-like letters with accompanying pointing. Label abstracts letter bodies only; no complete diplomatic transcription of pointing/accents or claim of four-letter יהוה.
observations.preservation: Name sign is on surviving paper, not reconstructed over a hole. Surrounding verse is abbreviated and locally damaged.
observations.inference: Supports the catalogue's identification of an abbreviated divine name at this slot.

observations.qualification: Prefixed lamed with comparable two-yod sign in the vow/payment context; MT/BHS has ליהוה. Some contextual words are abbreviated/damaged.
observations.inference: Local positive control for the type of divine-name abbreviation.

observations.qualification: Alef/dalet bodies appear at the left end of the preceding row; next row begins abbreviated דרש. The full word אדני is not written out. The initially named control77_3_name crop contains the following דרש row, not the decisive name; use priorline crop for the name.
observations.inference: Locally differs from target two-yod sign; weakens a claim that this scribe always uses the same sign for every Adonai token. Does not rule out occasional recitational substitution.

controls.wlc_edition: Repository OSHB/WLC Psalm XML, header WLC 4.20 update dated 2016-03-03; morphology release 2018-12-15. Modern derivative, not independent ancient witness.

pob_target.text: Will the Lord reject forever[a], and never again show favor?
pob_target.existing_note: Or, 'Will the Lord cast off forever, and never again be favorable?'
pob_target.current_disclosure: Lexical note, not Genizah/divine-name witness disclosure.

published.edition: Biblia Hebraica Stuttgartensia, fifth corrected edition, Schenker; copyright 1977/1997 Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft
published.consulted: Publisher's displayed selected Hebrew text, not critical apparatus
published.finding: Both print Adonai; WLC agrees locally. Not two independent Masoretic manuscript votes.
Prefixed Tetragrammaton ליהוה supplies the comparison slot.

published.consulted: Publisher's displayed selected Greek text, not critical apparatus or individual manuscript
published.finding: At target 76:8 the selected Greek has ἀπώσεται κύριος. At 76:3, corresponding to Hebrew 77:3, the selected Greek has τὸν θεὸν; this is a separate versional distinction, not a fresh Genizah variant.
κυρίῳ corresponds here to Hebrew ליהוה. Together with target κύριος, demonstrates why this Greek title alone cannot discriminate the proposed Hebrew name/title contrast.

published.edition: Institutional interview with Kim Phillips, by Melonie Schmierer-Lee; page shows August 25, 2021 and May 14, 2025
published.finding: Initial-word and initial-syllable abbreviation can function as recitation aids; accented-syllable forms can serve scribal reference purposes. General methodological support only; not a statement of AS67.19's specific purpose/date or a claim that its reading is late.

adjudication.attestation: Catalogue report strengthened by local image observation of a distinct abbreviation choice.
adjudication.can_distinguish: The surviving two-yod sign is not an alef/dalet word-initial abbreviation like the nearby Adonai control.
cannot_distinguish: A four-consonant יהוה exemplar versus a recitational/editorial divine-name sign substituted while abbreviating an Adonai exemplar.
The sign's entire vocalisation/accents with a certified diplomatic reading.
Earlier wording of the Psalm, from this undated-by-catalogue copy alone.
Independent manuscript support from the four associated shelfmarks.
adjudication.strongest_support: Name sign at target resembles same-leaf YHWH-slot convention and differs from nearby Adonai-slot abbreviation; Cambridge explicitly identifies the difference.
adjudication.strongest_contrary_explanation: A shorthand copy can normalize or substitute a divine-name sign at one occurrence through recitation or copying; a written abbreviation need not reproduce the exemplar's consonants. Nearby אד limits a universal-normalization explanation but does not eliminate occasional substitution.
adjudication.priority: Held. No dated chronological advantage established; no full critical apparatus or early witness comparison performed. No mechanical MT preference or shorter/older rule.
adjudication.reopening: Review abbreviation practices across catalogue-associated pieces, verify catalogue same-manuscript basis and date, seek full-word witnesses/apparatus for this precise locus, and obtain a genuinely independent/blinded image assessment before accepting fresh decipherment.

english_consequence.current: Retain the Lord provisionally; no canonical edit or new note applied.
english_consequence.conditional: If a future source adjudication selected יהוה here, project name policy would yield Yahweh rather than the Lord. This would be a source-wording/name decision, not an English-only modernization.
english_consequence.not_concluded: No claim that current Lord is demonstrably original, nor that a name change is justified by this image alone.

access_log: Web tool could not open CUDL item (safe-open/internal error); ordinary Chrome showed it and exposed public IIIF manifest. Public TEI/manifest/info/images downloaded without login or bypass.
An image-view attempt occurred before the first download finished and showed an incomplete JPEG; it was not used as evidence. After curl exited 0, both complete images were inspected and hashed.

Eight regional requests were selected from whole-image context, including supplementary regions because initial crops clipped relevant neighboring words. All were inspected; filenames are retrieval labels, not guaranteed locus contents.
No PDF read, no paywall circumvention, no OCR, no ImageGen, no stitching or enhancement. Native regions remained within advertised 2000×2000 service limits.
